text:
Ben Cho: Putting up a quick thread before drafting an RFC: mini-controlplane inside customer VPC vs regional broker. Wanted quick takes on trust surface, perf, and rollback.
Erin Zhao: Mini-CP = tiny agent that mints short-lived certs from signed tickets, right? Keeps latency low but holds ephemeral keys.
Alice Park: Yep. Pros: lower RTT for route/credential ops, better resilience for flaky links, useful for on-prem. Cons: install/upgrade burden and larger trust surface.
Carol Nguyen: Revocation is the tricky part. If mini-CP gets compromised we need fast revoke. Short TTLs + epoch digests might work but will increase poll load.
Ben Cho: Thinking constraints: no long-lived secrets in mini-CP, central issues signed time-limited tickets, mini-CP mints only short certs, central publishes epoch for revocation.
Erin Zhao: Broker alternative reduces installs and keeps trust central but still cuts RTT if placed near customer egress. Cost and infra ops higher.
Alice Park: Bootstrapping options: operator-run installer with one-time token, console-generated token, or CSR flow to customer CA. Need attestation for identity (instance identity / TPM).
Carol Nguyen: Observability and policy: require per-tenant metrics: ticket latency, renew rate, bootstrap failures, last-epoch. Also audit logs for bootstrap and operator actions.
Ben Cho: Fallbacks: agents must be able to fall back to central CP. Add config precedence and a timeout to avoid flapping. Also include a global kill-switch to force central-only mode.
Erin Zhao: Testing: chaos job to kill CP connectivity, rotate epoch, verify agent behavior and rollback path. Also simulate large-scale epoch increments to measure load.
Alice Park: I'll draft the RFC with API /claim /renew /revoke-epoch and a rollout checklist (alpha customers, metrics, kill-switch). Will include cost model for broker vs mini-CP.
infra-bot: Note created "mini-cp-proof" and assigned to infra-eng.
Carol Nguyen: One more: explicitly call out threat model and mitigations (attestation, short TTLs, signed responses).
Ben Cho: Great. Ping when draft is up and I'll add network cost numbers.
